evidence: register(router) only binds HTTP routes (POST /users, POST /projects, POST/GET /projects/:projectId/tasks, PATCH /tasks/:taskId/done), which is transport work.
createTask builds CreateTaskInput from request fields using requiredText/optionalText, then calls this.service.createTask. It only checks types and presence and makes no business decisions.
markDone calls this.service.markTaskDone. The rule that a task can't be completed twice stays in the domain (TaskAlreadyDoneError).
errorHandler only maps error types to HTTP statuses (InvalidInputError→400, TaskAlreadyDoneError→409, ResourceNotFoundError→404, else 500), which is transport-level error translation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts is an Express HTTP adapter, which is an infrastructure responsibility. It registers routes, reads the request body, query and route params, checks that inputs are well-formed (types and presence), passes the work to TaskService, and turns errors into HTTP status codes. None of this is business logic. Task status rules, assignment and completion are all left to the application and domain layers. The validation helpers only check request syntax and data types, which belongs at the transport boundary. errorHandler only turns error types into status codes (400, 409, 404, 500), which is presentation/transport mapping. The file does not access persistence directly and contains no domain decisions.
